title: Best Laptops UK
short: Windows, Mac and Chromebook laptops compared by performance, screen and battery life, from budget to gaming.
intro: The right laptop depends heavily on what you'll actually run on it, from browsing and email to gaming or creative work. This guide compares laptops tested by Expert Reviews, spanning budget Chromebooks to premium ultraportables and gaming machines.

products.name: MagicBook Pro 14 (2025)
products.best_for: Buyers who want workstation-level performance without workstation pricing
products.key_spec: Intel Core Ultra 9 285H, 32GB RAM, OLED, 16hr battery
products.summary: Expert Reviews' overall winner, offering what it calls workstation performance for a pittance, with an excellent OLED screen, though it's heavier than comparable laptops and lacks 6GHz Wi-Fi support.

products.name: MacBook Air 13in (M5, 2026)
products.best_for: Buyers who want a fast, reliable Mac laptop
products.key_spec: Apple M5, 16GB RAM, Liquid Retina, 15hr battery
products.summary: Fast performance, reliable build quality and long battery life, though it costs more than the previous M4 model and is less repairable than some rivals.
cons: Higher price than the M4 model

products.name: MacBook Neo
products.best_for: Buyers who want an affordable entry into the Mac ecosystem
products.summary: Apple's first proper budget laptop, offering excellent value in a sturdy, easy-to-repair aluminium chassis, though battery performance is disappointing and there's no keyboard backlight.

products.name: Chromebook Plus 14 Gen 10
products.best_for: Buyers who mainly need a browser-based laptop with real performance
products.summary: A lightweight Chromebook with a genuinely exceptional OLED screen and top-tier performance for the category, though the display is limited to Full HD and ports are limited.

products.name: Zenbook A14 (2025)
products.best_for: Buyers who want the lightest laptop with the longest battery life
products.summary: Weighs under 1kg with a vivid OLED display and exceptional battery endurance, making it well suited to travel, though the webcam is subpar and graphics performance is weak.

products.name: TUF Gaming A14 (2025)
products.best_for: Gamers who want strong performance without excessive bulk
products.summary: Strong gaming capability with solid battery life and dual SSD slots for expansion, though it uses Wi-Fi 6E rather than 7 and has no RGB keyboard lighting.
pros: Solid battery life for a gaming laptop

products.name: Zenbook S 14 (UX5406)
products.best_for: Windows buyers who want a premium ultraportable
products.summary: A premium, feature-rich ultraportable with extended battery life, though Expert Reviews notes the Core Ultra 9 underperforms relative to its price and the Core Ultra 7 version offers better value.
cons: Core Ultra 9 underperforms relative to price
Core Ultra 7 model offers better value

guide.a: Windows laptops offer the widest range of software and hardware options, including gaming. Macs pair tightly with Apple's ecosystem and often lead on battery life and build quality. Chromebooks are simpler, cheaper and well suited to browser-based tasks, but limited for demanding software.

guide.q: How much RAM do I need?
guide.a: 8GB is a practical minimum for everyday browsing and office work. 16GB suits multitasking and most creative work comfortably, while 32GB benefits heavier workloads like video editing or running multiple demanding applications at once.

guide.q: Do I need a dedicated graphics card?
guide.a: If you play modern games or do GPU-accelerated creative work like video editing, a dedicated GPU (like the RTX 5060 here) makes a big difference. For browsing, office work and streaming video, integrated graphics are usually enough.

guide.q: What battery life should I look for?
guide.a: Manufacturer-stated battery life is measured under specific conditions and real-world use is usually shorter. Look for laptops rated well above the battery life you actually need, and treat the figures here, which come from Expert Reviews' own testing, as a more realistic guide than marketing claims.
